column2: Retain the king's peaceful return to his own house in Jerusalem. This specifies Jehoshaphat's return rather than attributing Ahab's fate to both kings.
Retain Jehu son of Anani, the prophetic rebuke, helping a sinner and befriending someone hated by the Lord. The passive hated by the Lord is not changed to one who hates the Lord.
Retain the qualification good things, removal of groves from Judah and the heart directed to seeking the Lord. The rebuke and favorable acknowledgment both remain.
column3: Good things represents a broad use of words/matters; its precise scope is provisional.

column2: Retain residence in Jerusalem, renewed outreach from Beersabee to Ephraim's mountain and turning the people to their fathers' God. The geographical range is not reduced to Judah's fortified cities.
Retain judges appointed in all fortified cities, city by city. The distributive repetition matters for the extent of the appointments.
Retain judgment for the Lord rather than a human being and matters of judgment with the judges. Do not replace the latter clause with the Lord being with them, which is not its selected wording.
column3: Matters of judgment are with you remains provisional; the precise responsibility implied needs specialist review.

column2: Retain the Lord's fear, watchfulness and action, and the three exclusions: injustice, partiality expressed as admiration of a face, and accepting gifts. Status is an interpretation of the face idiom, not a separate Greek noun.
column3: The imperative/future sequence and a more natural equivalent for admiration of a person's status remain open.

column2: Retain some priests, Levites and ancestral rulers, the Lord's judgment, and judging Jerusalem's inhabitants. The final clause is not made a return to Jerusalem from another text.
Retain fear, truth and a full heart as three qualifications for judging. Full heart is not silently replaced with a narrower professional quality.

Restore the opening each-person expression by addressing each of the judges before the instruction about cases. Preserve blood and blood, the four legal categories, explicit future non-sinning and absence of wrath, and the final repeated command and assurance. The inherited text remains the close draft; the proposed literary syntax supplies of you from the judicial address.
column3: The nominative each person followed by accusative judgment and a plural verb is syntactically difficult. Its distributive attachment to the judges and the legal categories remain provisional; no exhaustive token review is claimed.

column2: Retain Amarias over matters of the Lord, Zabdias son of Ismael over royal matters, and both scribes and Levites before the judges. The Lord with the good remains broader than a promise exclusively to the addressees.
Retain Moab, Ammon and some Minaeans in the attacking coalition. Do not identify the third group with another people without evidence.
Retain the report from beyond the sea, specifically from Syria, and the equation Asasanthamar/Engaddi. Syria is not silently changed to Edom to resolve geography.
Retain Jehoshaphat's fear, setting his face to seek the Lord and the fast throughout Judah. His reaction includes seeking as well as public proclamation.
Retain both seeking clauses and the gathering from all Judah's cities. The repeated purpose is not compressed away.
Retain Judah's assembly in Jerusalem, the Lord's house and the new courtyard before which he stands. No additional assembly of Jerusalem is inserted.

Retain the appeal to the fathers' God, heavenly sovereignty over all national kingdoms, strength in His hand and inability to resist. Thou/Thy/Thee address God; English divides the extended rhetorical question into a question and affirmations.
column3: The shortened English question scope and mighty strength for the layered power phrase remain provisional stylistic choices.

column2: Retain the Lord's destruction of the former inhabitants before Israel and the enduring gift to Abraham's descendants, with Abraham His beloved. Beloved is not expanded to a distinct title friend.
Retain habitation in the land and the sanctuary built for Thy name. The following quoted prayer continues the direct divine address.

Retain calamity, sword, judgment, death and famine, standing before the house and God, His name upon the house, crying from affliction and future hearing and saving. Judgment is not silently absorbed into sword as an adjective.

Retain the coalition including Mount Seir, God's not permitting passage, Israel's departure from Egypt, turning aside and not destroying them. Divine Thou contrasts with the two human plural pronoun groups.
column3: The chain of plural antecedents remains contextually resolved rather than grammatically explicit in English names.

column2: Retain now/behold and their attempt to come out and expel the speakers from the inheritance God gave. The inheritance is ours here, not rewritten as God's possession.
Retain judging among them, inability to resist, not knowing what to do to them, and eyes upon God. The indirect object to them is not removed to match a familiar shorter prayer.
column3: Judge among them retains the selected preposition without deciding whether the idiom should be rendered judge them.

column2: Retain all Judah, their children and the women standing before the Lord. No distinct extra sons category is supplied.
Retain Oziel, Zacharias, Banaias, Eleel, Manthanias, Levite and Asaph ancestry, including plural sons in the chain. The Spirit of the Lord comes upon him in the assembly.
column3: The compressed ancestry's generational relationships and English name forms remain provisional.

column2: Retain the three addressed groups, emphatic you yourselves, both fear prohibitions and the battle array belonging to God. The Greek's contrast is preserved despite English reversing the two clauses for cadence.
Retain tomorrow, descent against the advancing force, ascent of Asas and the edge of the wilderness river of Jeriel. Do not substitute other place names from a parallel tradition.

Retain no need to fight, understand these things, see salvation, the named hearers, repeated fear prohibitions and going out tomorrow. Understand is not replaced with stand firm from another textual form.
Retain Jehoshaphat's face-down bow and the whole assembly falling before the Lord to worship Him. Both the physical action and its purpose remain.
Retain Levites from Kaath and Kore, standing to praise Israel's God and the high loud voice. The family groups are not flattened into unnamed singers.

Retain early departure to Thekoe, Jehoshaphat's shouted appeal, trust and the passive will be trusted, then singular His prophet and prosperity. Do not replace the passive with established or pluralize prophet.
column3: Will be trusted is lexically close but needs further contextual and spoken-language review.

column2: Retain consultation, singers and praisers, thanks and praise of the holy things, their position before the army and the two-clause thanksgiving. Add three display lines: narrative introduction followed by the two song clauses, with unchanged wording.
column3: Praise the holy things retains the selected object rather than substituting holy attire; its precise sense remains open.

column2: Retain the onset of praise, the Lord causing Ammon to fight against Moab and Mount Seir, and the rout. No unseen ambushers are inserted in place of the expressly named fighters.
column3: His in the praise phrase and the antecedent of the final plural rout remain open; capitalization is inherited and provisional.

column2: Retain Ammon and Moab against Seir, destruction and wiping out, completion of that attack and then reciprocal destruction. The changing coalition is not harmonized away.
Retain arrival at the wilderness lookout, the successive looking and seeing, all fallen dead and no survivor. Do not soften the reported extent of destruction.
Retain herds, baggage, spoils and desirable articles, acquisition for themselves and three days because of abundance. No corpses or inability to carry are imported from another text.
Retain fourth-day assembly, blessing the Lord and the named valley with its to-this-day explanation. Vale/Valley reflects the two selected topographical nouns without asserting two places.
Retain every man of Judah returning to Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat leading and great joy attributed to the Lord over their enemies. Do not add Jerusalem's men as a separate group.
Retain nablas, kinyras and trumpets and entry toward the Lord's house. Instrument identifications remain transliterated rather than falsely precise modern equivalents.
Retain terror from the Lord upon all kingdoms when they hear that He fought Israel's opponents. The causal report and divine military action remain explicit.
Retain the kingdom being at peace and God giving rest all around. The intransitive peace verb agrees with the revised handling at 14:4.
Retain accession at thirty-five, twenty-five years in Jerusalem and Azouba daughter of Sali. No adjustment is made to reconcile other chronological notices.
Retain Asa's ways and no turning aside from doing right before the Lord. The favorable evaluation precedes, rather than erases, the next qualification.
Retain high places still existing and the people's heart still not directed to their fathers' God. Do not harmonize this with the removal notice at 17:6.
Retain first and last acts, Jehu son of Anani and his writing down a book of Israel's kings. The relative clause makes him the writer rather than making his accounts simply incorporated into a book.
Retain partnership with Ahaziah and the parenthetic this man acted lawlessly. The demonstrative most naturally points to Ahaziah but the English does not replace it with a repeated name.
Retain the action/going-to-him sequence, construction for travel to Tharsis and ships made at Gasion-gaber. Tharsis is a destination in the selected text, not merely a ship class.
column3: The infinitival syntax and implicit singular builder remain unresolved beyond the inherited contextual reading.

column2: Retain Eliezer son of Dodia from Marisa, the friendship as cause, the Lord shattering the work, wrecked ships and his inability to travel. The final inability has a singular subject, not simply ships unable to sail.
